sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act)
sources.author_or_organisation: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
sources.jurisdiction: Europese Unie; rechtstreeks relevant voor Nederland
claims_supported: De AI Act is bindende, risicogebaseerde EU-regelgeving voor AI-systemen en bevat gefaseerde verplichtingen.
sources.reliability_notes: Originele tekst in het Publicatieblad via EUR-Lex; primaire rechtsbron.
sources.limitations: De originele tekst moet voor de actuele stand samen met latere wijzigingen en toepassingsdata worden gelezen.

sources.title: Consolidated text: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
sources.author_or_organisation: Publications Office of the European Union
sources.jurisdiction: Europese Unie; rechtstreeks relevant voor Nederland
claims_supported: De geconsolideerde tekst verwerkt de op 27 juli 2026 geldende wijzigingen in de AI Act.
sources.reliability_notes: Officiële EUR-Lex-consolidatie die de geldende tekst toegankelijk samenbrengt.
sources.limitations: Een geconsolideerde tekst heeft geen zelfstandige rechtskracht; bij juridische twijfel zijn de gepubliceerde wijzigingshandelingen leidend.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 amending Regulations (EU) 2024/1689, (EU) 2018/1139 and (EU) 2023/1230 as regards the simplification of the implementation of harmonised rules on artificial intelligence (Digital Omnibus on AI)
sources.author_or_organisation: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
sources.jurisdiction: Europese Unie; rechtstreeks relevant voor Nederland
claims_supported: De wijzigingsverordening vereenvoudigt de uitvoering van geharmoniseerde AI-regels en wijzigt uitsluitend de genoemde Verordeningen (EU) 2024/1689, 2018/1139 en 2023/1230.
sources.reliability_notes: Definitieve verordening in het Publicatieblad via EUR-Lex.
sources.limitations: Voor een concrete verplichting blijven de gewijzigde bepaling, overgangsregels en rol van de organisatie bepalend.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation)
sources.author_or_organisation: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
sources.jurisdiction: Europese Unie; rechtstreeks relevant voor Nederland
claims_supported: De AVG stelt bindende voorwaarden aan verwerking van persoonsgegevens, ook wanneer AI daarbij wordt ingezet.
sources.reliability_notes: Officiële tekst van de verordening via EUR-Lex; primaire rechtsbron.
sources.limitations: De toepasselijkheid en rechtmatigheid moeten per verwerking, rol en context worden beoordeeld; de bron bewijst geen AVG-conformiteit van een product.

sources.title: Opinion 28/2024 on certain data protection aspects related to the processing of personal data in the context of AI models
claims_supported: Anonimiteit, gerechtvaardigd belang en gevolgen van onrechtmatig verwerkte trainingsdata moeten bij AI-modellen contextspecifiek worden beoordeeld.
sources.reliability_notes: Formeel EDPB-advies op grond van artikel 64 AVG.
sources.limitations: Niet-bindende guidance en geen product- of sectorspecifieke conformiteitsbeslissing.

sources.title: Handreiking generatieve AI en de AVG
claims_supported: Organisaties die generatieve AI inzetten moeten hun rol, persoonsgegevensstromen, grondslag, risico's en rechten van betrokkenen expliciet beoordelen.
sources.reliability_notes: Actuele handreiking van de Nederlandse privacytoezichthouder.
sources.limitations: Algemene handreiking; geen juridisch oordeel over een specifieke onderwijsimplementatie.

sources.title: Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law (CETS No. 225)
sources.jurisdiction: Council of Europe; status must be checked for the Netherlands
claims_supported: The convention establishes an international treaty framework linking AI lifecycle activities to human rights, democracy and the rule of law.
sources.reliability_notes: Official treaty page with text and current signature and ratification status.
sources.limitations: The instrument is intended to be legally binding for parties after entry into force, but was not itself directly binding Dutch law at the verification date; country status remains time-sensitive.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
sources.author_or_organisation: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.jurisdiction: United States; internationally used voluntary framework
claims_supported: The AI RMF organises voluntary AI risk management around Govern, Map, Measure and Manage functions.
sources.reliability_notes: Official NIST publication developed through a public process.
sources.limitations: Voluntary and non-sector-specific; not proof of legal compliance or effective implementation. A revision was underway at verification.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
sources.author_or_organisation: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.jurisdiction: United States; internationally usable voluntary profile
claims_supported: The profile identifies risks and risk-management actions specific to generative AI within the AI RMF structure.
sources.reliability_notes: Official NIST companion profile with explicit risk taxonomy and actions.
sources.limitations: Voluntary, not education-specific and not a certification or assurance result.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 Information technology - Artificial intelligence - Management system
claims_supported: ISO/IEC 42001 specifies requirements for an organisational AI management system.
sources.reliability_notes: Canonical ISO catalogue entry for the published standard.
sources.limitations: Voluntary and paywalled; using or certifying against it does not by itself prove AI Act conformity or responsible outcomes.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 23894:2023 Information technology - Artificial intelligence - Guidance on risk management
claims_supported: ISO/IEC 23894 provides guidance for integrating AI-specific risks into organisational risk management.
sources.reliability_notes: Canonical ISO catalogue entry for the published standard.
sources.limitations: Voluntary, generic and paywalled; it does not determine sector-specific acceptability or legal compliance.

sources.title: EN 18286:2026 Artificial intelligence - Quality management system for EU AI Act regulatory purposes
claims_supported: EN 18286:2026 specifies a quality-management-system framework for organisations providing AI systems in support of EU AI Act regulatory purposes.
sources.reliability_notes: Official CEN project record for the published European standard.
sources.limitations: At verification it was not cited in the Official Journal as a harmonised standard, so no presumption of AI Act conformity may be inferred; this status can change.

sources.title: Standardisation of the AI Act
claims_supported: The Commission page explains the role and changing status of harmonised standards under the AI Act.
sources.reliability_notes: Current European Commission policy page on the standardisation process.
sources.limitations: Process information is time-sensitive and does not itself designate every listed standard as harmonised.

sources.title: Multilayer Framework for Good Cybersecurity Practices for AI
claims_supported: AI cybersecurity controls can be organised across foundational IT, AI-system and sector-specific layers.
sources.reliability_notes: Technical synthesis by the EU cybersecurity agency.
sources.limitations: Good-practice framework rather than outcome evaluation, audit result or binding requirement.

sources.title: ENISA's view on cybersecurity in the frontier AI era
claims_supported: Frontier AI changes the threat landscape and creates both new cybersecurity capabilities and dependencies.
sources.reliability_notes: Recent strategic assessment by the EU cybersecurity agency.
sources.limitations: Forward-looking and rapidly evolving; not a quantified forecast or education-specific risk assessment.

sources.title: Empowering Learners for the Age of AI: An AI Literacy Framework for Primary and Secondary Education
claims_supported: The framework proposes a structured set of AI-literacy competencies for learners in primary and secondary education.
sources.reliability_notes: Final joint OECD-European Commission framework based on expert and stakeholder development.
sources.limitations: Normative competence framework, not an effectiveness study or mandatory curriculum.

sources.title: DigComp 3.0: The Digital Competence Framework for Citizens
claims_supported: DigComp 3.0 provides a current European reference framework for digital competence, including competence in AI-mediated contexts.
sources.reliability_notes: Official JRC framework; successor to DigComp 2.2.
sources.limitations: Reference framework rather than a validated intervention or mandatory educational standard.

sources.title: Guidelines on the ethical use of artificial intelligence and data in teaching and learning for educators
sources.author_or_organisation: European Commission, Directorate-General for Education, Youth, Sport and Culture
claims_supported: Educators can use structured questions and safeguards to assess ethical and data-related implications of AI in teaching and learning.
sources.reliability_notes: Updated official European Commission guidance for educators.
sources.limitations: Non-binding guidance and not evidence that a specific tool or teaching method is effective or lawful.

sources.title: Council conclusions on teachers in the era of artificial intelligence (AI)
claims_supported: The Council calls for sustained support, professional development and human-centred conditions for teachers and trainers using AI.
sources.reliability_notes: Official Council conclusions published in the Official Journal.
sources.limitations: Political conclusions are non-binding and do not demonstrate implementation or impact in member states.

sources.title: Recommendation CM/Rec(2026)12 on AI literacy
sources.author_or_organisation: Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe
claims_supported: The recommendation frames AI literacy as a public capability linked to human rights, democracy and the rule of law.
sources.reliability_notes: Official recommendation adopted by the Council of Europe's Committee of Ministers.
sources.limitations: Non-binding and very recent; national implementation and practical outcomes remain unverified.

sources.title: Guidance for generative AI in education and research
claims_supported: A human-centred policy approach to generative AI should address agency, inclusion, privacy, age appropriateness and pedagogical purpose.
sources.reliability_notes: Official UNESCO global guidance synthesising policy considerations.
sources.limitations: Normative guidance, not a causal evaluation of learning or a jurisdiction-specific legal interpretation.

sources.title: AI competency framework for teachers
claims_supported: The framework organises teacher AI competencies across human-centred, ethical, technical and pedagogical dimensions.
sources.reliability_notes: Canonical UNESCO publication with persistent DOI.
sources.limitations: Non-binding competence framework; not evidence of learning impact or implementation quality.

sources.title: AI competency framework for students
claims_supported: The framework defines student AI competencies for responsible, creative and human-centred participation.
sources.reliability_notes: Canonical UNESCO Digital Library record.
sources.limitations: Non-binding competence framework; not a validated curriculum or effectiveness study.

sources.title: OECD Digital Education Outlook 2026
claims_supported: Better AI-assisted task performance cannot automatically be treated as evidence of durable learning.
sources.reliability_notes: OECD evidence synthesis that separates immediate performance from learning and system conditions.
sources.limitations: Broad policy synthesis; causal claims depend on the underlying studies and contexts.

sources.title: PISA 2025 Results (Volume I): Future-Ready Students
claims_supported: PISA 2025 reports associations between forms of AI use, AI literacy, educational outcomes and socioeconomic differences.
sources.reliability_notes: Large international OECD assessment with documented methods and comparative data.
sources.limitations: The AI-use analyses are largely cross-sectional and self-reported; associations are not causal effects of AI use.

sources.title: Guidance on AI and children, version 3.0
claims_supported: AI policy and design affecting children should address safety, privacy, fairness, transparency, inclusion and children's agency.
sources.reliability_notes: Current UNICEF policy guidance focused specifically on children's rights.
sources.limitations: Non-binding global guidance; local law, age groups and use contexts require separate assessment.

sources.title: AI-GO! Een raamwerk voor AI-geletterdheid in het onderwijs
claims_supported: AI-GO! offers a Dutch education-oriented framework for structuring AI literacy.
sources.reliability_notes: Sector programme publication that synthesises and adapts concepts for Dutch educational practice.
sources.limitations: The framework is not an effect study, legal norm or independent validation of institutional maturity.

sources.title: Visie op toetsing, examinering en AI: handreikingen
claims_supported: Assessment policy under AI conditions requires explicit choices about learning goals, permitted use, validity and examination design.
sources.reliability_notes: Practice-oriented guidance from the Dutch Npuls programme.
sources.limitations: Sector guidance rather than binding regulation or comparative evidence of effectiveness.

sources.title: Werken met het raamwerk AI-geletterdheid
claims_supported: Kennisnet translates AI-literacy concepts into a practical framework for Dutch schools.
sources.reliability_notes: Recent practice-oriented publication by the Dutch public education ICT expertise organisation.
sources.limitations: Adaptation in active development; not a mandatory standard or independent impact evaluation.

sources.title: Startverkenning Generatieve Artificiële Intelligentie: Thematische analyse kwaliteitszorg
sources.author_or_organisation: Accreditation Organisation of the Netherlands and Flanders
claims_supported: The scan documents how generative AI questions appear in Dutch higher-education quality-assurance materials.
sources.reliability_notes: Primary institutional document analysis by the Dutch-Flemish accreditation organisation.
sources.limitations: Exploratory scan; it does not establish prevalence beyond the analysed documents or causal effects on quality.

sources.title: Evidence of impact and interpretational limits of generative AI in STEM education: a systematic review and meta-analysis on cognitive learning outcomes
sources.author_or_organisation: Chiara Boolzen, Jochen Kuhn, Salome Flegr, Eva-Maria Rott, Niklas Stausberg and Stefan Küchemann
sources.jurisdiction: International; mainly higher education and text-based GenAI in STEM
claims_supported: Reported GenAI learning effects are extremely heterogeneous and shrink to near zero under a robust Bayesian publication-bias correction; augmentation appears more promising than replacement of learner activity.
sources.reliability_notes: PRISMA review with double screening, risk-of-bias assessment and explicit publication-bias analysis across 85 studies.
sources.limitations: No included study had low overall risk of bias; English-language STEM evidence only, search ended May 2026 and heterogeneity remained largely unexplained.

sources.title: Does ChatGPT enhance student learning? A systematic review and meta-analysis of experimental studies
sources.author_or_organisation: Ruiqi Deng, Maoli Jiang, Xinlu Yu, Yuyan Lu and Shasha Liu
sources.jurisdiction: International; predominantly higher and language education
claims_supported: The experimental literature reports positive average effects for performance, affect and some higher-order outcomes, alongside high heterogeneity and no significant self-efficacy effect.
sources.reliability_notes: Meta-analysis of 69 experimental studies with several learning-related outcome families.
sources.limitations: High heterogeneity, short-term outcomes, limited power analyses and some post-tests with ChatGPT still available can conflate task performance with learning.

sources.title: Effect of generative artificial intelligence on university students learning outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis
sources.author_or_organisation: Shuzhen Chen and Alan C. K. Cheung
claims_supported: The higher-education literature reports positive pooled effects for several outcomes but no significant pooled metacognition effect.
sources.reliability_notes: Higher-education-specific synthesis of 57 studies and 97 estimates.
sources.limitations: Interventions and measures differ substantially; moderator associations are observational and results do not generalise beyond university contexts.

sources.title: Effectiveness of Intelligent Tutoring Systems: A Meta-Analytic Review
sources.author_or_organisation: James A. Kulik and J. D. Fletcher
claims_supported: Classical intelligent tutoring systems showed a median achievement improvement, with estimates sensitive to test type, implementation quality and comparator design.
sources.reliability_notes: Meta-analytic review of 50 controlled evaluations; useful historical baseline.
sources.limitations: Older bounded tutors differ materially from open-ended LLMs, and locally developed tests can overestimate effects.

sources.title: Teacher intervention in K-12 AI-based instruction: a systematic review of processes, strategies, and effects
sources.jurisdiction: International K-12; evidence concentrated in US and STEM settings
claims_supported: Teacher monitoring, judgement, intervention and orchestration remain central to making AI information pedagogically usable.
sources.reliability_notes: PRISMA review of 29 studies across six databases with quality assessment and double coding checks.
sources.limitations: Many effects are perceptual or indirect, teacher effects are hard to isolate, AI types are pooled and evidence is geographically and disciplinarily concentrated.

sources.title: Understanding privacy and data protection issues in learning analytics using a systematic review
claims_supported: Privacy and data-protection issues occur throughout the learning-analytics lifecycle, while applied evidence that proposed remedies work remains limited.
sources.reliability_notes: Systematic review of 47 articles across four databases.
sources.limitations: Learning analytics is broader than GenAI and the review is not a jurisdiction-specific legal analysis.

sources.title: Algorithmic Bias in Education
sources.author_or_organisation: Ryan S. Baker and Aaron Hawn
sources.jurisdiction: International literature; evidence concentrated in the United States
claims_supported: Educational algorithms can produce unequal treatment across groups and bias can enter at multiple stages of the machine-learning lifecycle.
sources.reliability_notes: Influential structured review focused on empirical manifestations of bias in education.
sources.limitations: Pre-GenAI, not a PRISMA meta-analysis, geographically concentrated and sparse for disability, socioeconomic status and intersectional effects.

sources.title: AI tutoring outperforms in-class active learning: an RCT introducing a novel research-based design in an authentic educational setting
sources.author_or_organisation: Greg Kestin, Kelly Miller, Anna Klales, Timothy Milbourne and Gregorio Ponti
claims_supported: A carefully engineered subject-specific AI tutor produced larger immediate learning gains in less time than the active-learning comparison in this bounded setting.
sources.reliability_notes: Randomised crossover design with pre- and post-tests, prior-knowledge and time controls, and available data.
sources.limitations: Two lessons at one elite institution with immediate post-tests and expert-built materials; no evidence for generic ChatGPT, long-term retention or teacher replacement.

sources.title: Generative AI without guardrails can harm learning: Evidence from high school mathematics
sources.author_or_organisation: Hamsa Bastani, Osbert Bastani, Alp Sungu, Haosen Ge, Özge Kabakcı and Rei Mariman
sources.jurisdiction: One large Turkish secondary school; mathematics; four sessions
claims_supported: Unguided GPT-4 improved assisted practice performance but reduced later AI-free test performance; a guardrailed tutor improved practice without a significant AI-free test difference from control.
sources.reliability_notes: Large preregistered cluster randomised field experiment with independent grading and an AI-free primary outcome.
sources.limitations: One school, one subject, short duration and a 2023 model; the guardrails depended on labour-intensive teacher-authored solutions and error patterns.

sources.title: ChatGPT as a cognitive crutch: Evidence from a randomized controlled trial on knowledge retention
claims_supported: In this trial, the ChatGPT study group scored lower than traditional study on an unexpected AI-free retention test after 45 days.
sources.reliability_notes: Individual randomisation and a relatively rare delayed, AI-free outcome measure.
sources.limitations: High attrition with complete-case analysis, one programme and country, one author, no blinding and no measurement of broader transfer or autonomy.

sources.title: GPT detectors are biased against non-native English writers
sources.author_or_organisation: Weixin Liang, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yining Mao, Eric Wu and James Zou
claims_supported: The tested GPT detectors produced high false-positive rates for non-native English writing and could also be evaded by rewriting.
sources.reliability_notes: Direct and reproducible fairness and robustness benchmark with known document provenance.
sources.limitations: Small unmatched English corpora and 2023 detector versions; the study demonstrates a risk, not every product's current error rate.

sources.title: Testing of detection tools for AI-generated text
sources.author_or_organisation: Debora Weber-Wulff, Alla Anohina-Naumeca, Sonja Bjelobaba, Tomáš Foltýnek, Jean Guerrero-Dib, Olumide Popoola, Petr Šigut and Lorna Waddington
claims_supported: The tested AI-text detectors showed false positives, false negatives and strong sensitivity to paraphrasing, making detector output unsuitable as sole evidence of misconduct.
sources.reliability_notes: Comparative test of fourteen tools with known-ground-truth human, translated, AI-generated and edited documents.
sources.limitations: Snapshot of 2023 tools and one ChatGPT model snapshot; small document set and no systematic test of iterative hybrid writing or current versions.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on harmonised rules on fair access to and use of data
sources.author_or_organisation: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
sources.jurisdiction: Europese Unie; rechtstreeks relevant voor Nederland
claims_supported: De Data Act stelt bindende regels over eerlijke toegang tot en gebruik van data en is sinds 12 september 2025 van toepassing, met specifieke overgangsbepalingen.
sources.reliability_notes: Officiële Nederlandstalige tekst van de verordening via EUR-Lex.
sources.limitations: De concrete toepasselijkheid hangt af van product, rol, datatype en overgangsbepaling; de bron is geen sectorspecifieke implementatiehandleiding.

sources.title: Digital Education Action Plan 2021-2027 - COM(2020) 624 final
claims_supported: Het Digital Education Action Plan is een niet-bindend EU-beleidsactieplan voor digitaal onderwijs en digitale vaardigheden.
sources.reliability_notes: Officiële mededeling van de Europese Commissie via EUR-Lex.
sources.limitations: Het plan bevat beleidsdoelen en acties, geen rechtstreeks bindende verplichtingen of bewijs van nationale uitvoering.

sources.title: Nederlandse gedragscode wetenschappelijke integriteit 2018
sources.author_or_organisation: KNAW, NFU, NWO, TO2-federatie, Vereniging Hogescholen en VSNU
sources.jurisdiction: Nederland; onderzoeksinstellingen die de code onderschrijven
claims_supported: De gedragscode formuleert vijf principes en normen voor goede onderzoekspraktijken en zorgplichten van onderzoeksinstellingen.
sources.reliability_notes: Permanente DOI naar de officiële versie 1.0 van de nationale gedragscode.
sources.limitations: Geen wet; normatieve werking volgt uit onderschrijving en institutionele regelingen. Relevantie voor concreet AI-gebruik vraagt nadere duiding.
